title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: GAR all by permission—yet occult counsel not ordinary nature
pass_a_gloss: GAR presses that nothing at all in the government of the whole world happens with God unknowing or unwilling, without his permission, without his wisdom shining, or without just administration from unmoved rectitude—yet no one therefore says tree-growth, flowered meadows, animal propagation, or worms formed from earth come from occult, admirable, inscrutable counsel; those are ordinary most-right providence. Scripture reserves just, occult, marvelous counsel for singular dispensation and economy in certain works, as when Paul at Rom. 11:33 calls God's judgments inscrutable and his ways past finding out.
pass_b_english: GAR. What of this—that there is nothing at all in the government of the whole world that is done with God unknowing or unwilling, that happens without God's permission, where God's wisdom does not shine, that is not administered justly, that is, from God's unmoved and undeflected rectitude? Yet no one will therefore say these things are done from God's occult, just, admirable, inscrutable counsel even when trees grow, and meadows are varied with flowers, and animals propagate their species, and worms are formed from the earth. For those things certainly are all from wisdom and providence, and that most right and most consulted. But Scripture is accustomed to refer God's just, occult, marvelous counsel not to the common administration of such created things, but to a singular dispensation and economy in certain works: as when Paul says, Rom. 11:33, that God's judgments are inscrutable and his ways past finding out.
source_text: GAR. Quid quod nihil est omnino in totius mundi gubernatione, quod inscio, vel invito Deo fiat, quod sine permissione Dei eveniat, ubi non Dei sapientia eluceat, quod non juste, id est, ex immota & indeflexa Dei rectitudine administretur? Neque tamen propterea dicet aliquis haec fieri ex occulto, justo, admirabili, inscrutabili, Dei consilio, etiam cum arbores crescunt, & prata variegantur floribus, & animalia propagant speciem, & vermes ex terra formantur. Sunt enim certe illa omnia ex sapientia & providentia, eaque rectissima & consultissima. Sed justum, occultum, mirabile Dei consilium, non ad communem eiusmodi rerum creatarum administrationem Scriptura referre solet, sed ad singularem in certis operibus dispensationem & oeconomiam: ut cum dicit Paulus Roman. XI. 33. judicia Dei esse inscrutabilia, & vias eius impervestigabiles.
